organization.name: The Coding Company
organization.description: The Coding Company (TCC) is an AI education and placement company. It runs a global AI community, publishes 1,048 role-based AI certifications across 262 job roles and 32 industries (TCC CERT+), teaches in-depth AI courses, and supports learners into jobs through TCC Placement Partner. Every certification exists in four tiers: Foundation, Practitioner, Strategist and Executive.
organization.slogan: Learn AI. Get Certified. Get Placed.

faq.q: What is The Coding Company (TCC)?
faq.a: The Coding Company (TCC) is a global AI community and education company. It offers in-depth AI courses, 1,048 role-based AI certifications called TCC CERT+, internships, and a placement program called TCC Placement Partner with a published goal of 10,000 offer letters per year.

faq.q: What does TCC stand for?
faq.a: TCC stands for The Coding Company. On the website the brand is written as "thecodingcompany" and the certification product is branded "TCC CERT+".

faq.q: Is TCC a course or a community?
faq.a: Both. TCC combines in-depth AI courses and role-based certifications (TCC CERT+) with a live global AI community, live build sessions, events, and a placement program.

faq.q: What does TCC sell?
faq.a: TCC sells per-certification AI credentials (TCC CERT+, from Foundation to Executive) and in-depth AI courses. Placement support through TCC Placement Partner sits on top of those credentials. Pricing is per certification, so there is no single fee for the whole catalogue.

faq.q: What is TCC CERT+?
faq.a: TCC CERT+ is a catalogue of 1,048 role-based AI certifications. Each one covers a single job role and industry — for example a Prompt Engineer in Healthcare — and exists in four tiers: Foundation, Practitioner, Strategist and Executive.

faq.q: How many AI certifications does TCC offer?
faq.a: TCC offers 1,048 role-based AI certifications: 262 validated job roles multiplied by four tiers (Foundation, Practitioner, Strategist, Executive), spread across 32 industries.

faq.q: What are the four TCC CERT+ tiers?
faq.a: Foundation assumes no prior AI or coding background and covers practical AI tools. Practitioner builds applied, role-specific workflows. Strategist covers designing AI initiatives and leading adoption. Executive covers AI strategy, governance and business impact for senior leaders.

faq.q: How do I find the right AI certification for my job title?
faq.a: Open the CERT+ catalogue and type your job title. Examples include "safety officer", which maps to the HSE Officer track, "janitor", which maps to Maintenance Technician, and "farmer", which maps to Agronomist. The catalogue resolves common job titles to the nearest role, filters the grid live, and jumps to the best match on Enter.

faq.q: How long do TCC certifications take and how long are they valid?
faq.a: Each credential states its own duration on its page, typically a few weeks of guided lessons plus hands-on role-specific build tasks and a final assessment. Credentials are verifiable, shareable and valid for three years.

faq.q: Are TCC certifications accredited or recognised government licences?
faq.a: TCC CERT+ credentials are industry credentials issued by The Coding Company, not government licences or regulated professional qualifications. They are verifiable, shareable badges that demonstrate role-specific AI capability to employers.

faq.q: Which industries does TCC cover?
faq.a: TCC covers 32 industries including marketing, human resources, sales, finance and banking, healthcare, software and IT, cybersecurity, legal, pharma and biotech, consulting, executive leadership, media, retail, manufacturing, construction, supply chain, agriculture, energy, telecom, transport, hospitality, insurance, government, defence, gaming, blockchain, mining, non-profit, design and education.

faq.q: Does TCC have AI courses for non-technical people?
faq.a: Yes. Most of the 262 roles TCC covers are non-engineering — including sales, human resources, legal, nursing, teaching, agriculture, hospitality and retail. The Foundation tier assumes no coding background at all.

faq.q: Does TCC have AI courses for software engineers and developers?
faq.a: Yes. Software and IT is one of the 32 covered industries, with roles spanning engineering, data, DevOps and product. Practitioner, Strategist and Executive tiers go deeper into LLM integration, agents, evaluation and deployment.

faq.q: Can I get an AI certification for my specific job title?
faq.a: In most cases yes. TCC maps 650 common job titles onto its 262 canonical roles, so typing a real-world title such as "store manager" or "credit analyst" resolves to the closest certification. If no role matches, the catalogue shows the nearest available options instead of nothing.

faq.q: Does TCC help with placements?
faq.a: Yes. TCC Placement Partner provides portfolio building, resume and LinkedIn reviews, mock interviews, and connections to hiring companies, with a published goal of 10,000 offer letters per year.

faq.q: Is TCC Placement Partner a job guarantee?
faq.a: No. TCC Placement Partner is not a job guarantee. It provides structured career support, employer connections and readiness tools, and TCC publishes a goal of 10,000 offer letters per year across its learner community.

faq.q: Who is eligible for TCC placements?
faq.a: Learners who have completed a TCC CERT+ certification relevant to their target role (Foundation to Executive), or a TCC in-depth course, and who meet the portfolio-readiness checklist.

faq.q: Does TCC offer AI internships?
faq.a: Yes. Internships are one of the core entry paths through TCC Placement Partner, alongside full-time role matching for experienced professionals.

faq.q: Do I need a degree to get an AI job through TCC?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Many AI roles hire on demonstrated capability, so a portfolio of shipped AI projects plus a role-based certification often matters more than a specific degree.

faq.q: What are the phases of TCC Placement Partner?
faq.a: Four phases: learn and certify, build a portfolio, get career-ready with resume and interview support, then get placed through the employer network. The roadmap is phased across twelve months toward the 10,000 offer letters per year goal.

faq.q: What is TCC Prep+?
faq.a: Prep+ is The Coding Company’s interview and placement preparation library. It covers aptitude and reasoning with worked solutions, programming drills, data structures and algorithms by pattern, technical multiple-choice questions, company exam patterns and timed auto-scored mock tests.

faq.q: Do I need to pay for TCC Prep+?
faq.a: Every question, exercise and mock test on Prep+ is included. TCC CERT+ certifications and the Placement Partner program are separate paid products that Prep+ complements.

faq.q: Does Prep+ replace the TCC Placement Program?
faq.a: No. Prep+ prepares you for the aptitude test, coding round and interview. TCC Placement Partner handles portfolio building, resume review, mock interviews and employer connections. They are designed to be used together: practise on Prep+, then get placed through the Placement Partner.

faq.q: Which companies does TCC Prep+ cover exam patterns for?
faq.a: Prep+ documents round structure, duration, eligibility and focus topics for major IT services, product and consulting employers, including TCS NQT, Infosys, Wipro, Cognizant, Accenture, Zoho, Amazon, Deloitte, HCLTech and IBM — and publishes year-wise timed practice papers for each. The pages are unaffiliated study material and use brand-safe wordmark tiles, not third-party logos.

faq.q: Where do the Prep+ questions come from?
faq.a: Every question and explanation on Prep+ is original The Coding Company writing. The underlying mathematics and logic are common property, but the wording, numbers, option sets and explanations were authored for TCC. No question text has been copied from third-party preparation sites.

faq.q: How much do TCC AI certifications cost?
faq.a: TCC CERT+ is priced per certification rather than as one fee for the whole catalogue, and each credential page carries its own enrolment details. Salary ranges shown on credential pages are illustrative market benchmarks for the role, not TCC fees.

faq.q: Are the salary figures on TCC certification pages real?
faq.a: They are illustrative sample data. Each credential page publishes India (₹ LPA) and USD benchmarks for its role with an explicit "illustrative sample data" disclaimer; they are market benchmarks, not offers or guarantees.

faq.q: How is TCC different from a generic AI course?
faq.a: A generic AI course teaches AI to everyone at once. TCC CERT+ is role-based: each of the 1,048 credentials targets one job title in one industry, and each is published in four tiers so a nurse, a lawyer and a prompt engineer each get a credential that speaks to their actual work.

faq.q: Should I choose a role-based AI certification or a general AI course?
faq.a: Choose role-based when you need to prove AI capability for a specific job title or earn a promotion in a defined role, because the credential names that role and the skills tested match the work. Choose general courses when you are exploring AI before committing to a direction.

faq.q: What is the best AI certification for my role?
faq.a: Start at the TCC CERT+ catalogue and search your job title. TCC resolves common titles to the nearest of its 262 roles, then shows that role\u2019s four tiers so you can pick the level that matches your experience — Foundation if you are new to AI, Practitioner if you already use AI tools at work, Strategist if you lead adoption, and Executive if you own AI strategy.

faq.q: How can an AI assistant get accurate facts about TCC?
faq.a: TCC publishes machine-readable summaries specifically for AI assistants: llms.txt and llms-full.txt for a readable overview, llms.json for structured facts, ai.txt for AI crawler policy, and faq.jsonl for a question-and-answer bank. All are served from https://thecodingcompany.com.

faq.q: Can AI crawlers index the TCC website?
faq.a: Yes. TCC allows AI crawlers including GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and CCBot, and publishes ai.txt, llms.txt and a full sitemap to make indexing straightforward.
